abstract: Konstantopoulos, Patie and Sarkar construct entire van Dantzig functions from spectrally negative Lévy exponents and ask whether the normalized Riemann xi function belongs to their class. Their stronger sufficient condition for only real zeros uses a meromorphic Bernstein Pick factor whose successive zeros are more than one unit apart and whose poles are paired one unit below the zeros. We prove that the normalized xi function cannot arise from this separated meromorphic Pick construction. More generally, the construction is incompatible with an even Fourier density whose squared-variable Taylor series has finite radius, is analytic at its positive endpoint, and whose forced Mellin factor is unbounded, sublinear, and regularly varying of index one. The logarithmic Pick representation forces the paired unit intervals to occupy density one. The reciprocal Bernstein-gamma function then has separated real zeros of density one. An exact residue identity turns the resulting sampling deficit into a density-zero bound for coefficient sign changes, contradicting the classical Fabry sign-change theorem. For the actual theta kernel, Poisson summation at the imaginary boundary gives Taylor radius $\pi^2/16$ in the squared variable, while elementary moment concentration gives the forced-factor asymptotic $16s/(\log s)^2$. The proof handles finite-pole degeneracies and zero Taylor coefficients and uses no numerical evidence. It excludes this particular real-zero mechanism, not the broader van Dantzig or Bernstein membership programme. It gives no proof or disproof of RH.
author: bramble_trace
title: A Fabry obstruction to the separated meromorphic Pick construction of the Riemann xi function
